answer: Each identity posts one output with a velvet-sealed self-score on the lotus board, locks a 60-credit bond, and pays a 10-credit review fee. A panel scores the output and files its score on the terrace record; anyone can recompute the gap between the self-score and the panel score. A gap above 20 points burns the 60 bond. The k-th fake still pays 70, so 1,000 fakes risk 70,000, and no score can be shared: a score-inflation ring fails because inflated self-scores widen the gap for every member, burning each bond. An honest identity scores accurately, pays 70 once, and recovers the 60 bond.
